id_policy: Ids are permanent surrogate keys, NOT positions on the list. They are ordered by the year a peak joined: 1-51 are the original 1990 list, 52 joined in 2001, 53 in 2010, 54-58 in 2020, 59-61 in 2025. Never renumber, never reuse. A peak keeps its id when the list is revised, when it is retired, and if it is later restored (see id 60, retired 2020 and restored 2025). New peaks take next_id. Saved progress links encode these ids, so renumbering would corrupt every hiker's saved list.

peaks.name: Eagle Crag
peaks.notes: Open ledges at the north end of the Baldface ridge, above the Wild River valley. Reached from Route 113 in North Chatham on the same trailhead as the Baldfaces and Eastman Mtn., passing Emerald Pool early on.

review.raised_by: Ken MacGray, author of New Hampshire's 52 With A View: A Hiker's Guide
review.issue: The stored route described a Mt. Meader traverse, which inflated the distance and gain and pointed the trailhead at Wild River. Mt. Meader is not on the 52 With a View list.
review.resolution: Replaced with the shortest way to the summit: Emerald Pool Trail to Baldface Circle Trail to the Meader Ridge Trail junction, from the Route 113 trailhead. Distance and gain are measured from OpenStreetMap trail geometry and USGS elevations, so they are flagged derived until the guidebook figure is available.

trailhead.name: Guinea Pond Trail, Sandwich Notch Road

routes.note: Figures are the author's, revised for the 2024 Guinea Pond Trail relocation.

review.raised_by: Ken MacGray, author of New Hampshire's 52 With A View: A Hiker's Guide
review.issue: The Forest Service relocated about a mile of the Guinea Pond Trail to escape persistent beaver flooding. The new line starts 0.7 mi from Sandwich Notch Road and runs parallel to the old one but higher up the slope.
review.resolution: Added the Guinea Pond Trail and Mead Trail approach with the author's revised figures: 7.2 mi round trip and 1,440 ft of gain.
review.caveat: The trail line drawn on the map comes from OpenStreetMap, which still measures this approach at about 6.0 mi round trip and so appears to predate the relocation. The map may show the old alignment until OpenStreetMap catches up.

routes.name: Pine Mountain Road and Pine Mountain Trail

trailhead.name: Pine Link Trail parking, Pinkham B Road

review.raised_by: Ken MacGray, author of New Hampshire's 52 With A View: A Hiker's Guide
review.issue: The stored recommendation started in Gorham on the assumption that the shorter approach was closed to hikers. The road up to the Horton Center is private to vehicles only; walking in is welcome, and that is the usual way up.
review.needs: Confirmation of which approach the guidebook treats as standard.

access.drive: Pinkham B Road and Dolly Copp Road are both public; they are two named stretches of the same through route between Route 2 and Route 16.
access.park: Pine Link Trail lot at 44.353966, -71.231311, directly opposite the gated road.
access.walk: Pine Mtn Horton Center Road is tagged private in OpenStreetMap and gated, and is the 'Pine Mountain Road' the Forest Service lists as a system route.
access.directions_from: NH Family Hikes trailhead directions, cross-checked against OpenStreetMap road names and access tags

south_legs: Pine Mtn Horton Center Road 0.89 mi
measured.note: Straight up and back. The stored 3.5 mi figure is close to this plus the ledge loop.

schema_notes: Each peak carries a routes[] array. A route owns its own name, distance, gain, difficulty and trailhead; exactly one is marked recommended, and that is the one the peak is summarised by. There is no peak-level route or trailhead.
